prompt: A line of small round buoys strung on a thin rope crossing the open sea in a gentle rising diagonal, seen from slightly above. Partway along, a second thin rope with its own few buoys clearly branches off to one side, runs beside the main rope for a stretch and rejoins it further on, forming a long narrow loop. The last buoy, at the upper right end, carries a little cobalt blue #3D6FD9 pennant flag on a thin mast with a bold off-white check mark on it. Buoys and ropes drawn in crisp off-white and ink grey line art with fine engraved shading, small ripples drawn as lines around each buoy. Richly detailed engraved nautical chart style, like a fine antique sea chart printed in two inks: the sea built from many layers of fine wave lines and hatching, line density increasing towards the deep water to give depth, tonal bands from deep cerulean at the bottom to lighter cerulean at the top, bathymetric contour lines with small depth soundings drawn as tiny dots, a delicate compass rose with fine tick marks in a corner, subtle foam strokes and a few glints of light on the crests. Every wave is drawn as visible engraved line work, like a steel engraving, never painted, never smooth. Crisp sharp lines of several weights, intricate but calm, premium print quality, high detail, elegant. No realistic objects, no photographic rendering, no glow, no text, no letters, no numbers, no watermark, no horizon, no sky, no clouds, full-bleed edge to edge, no border, no frame, the buoys in the upper two thirds and towards the right, open water on the left and along the bottom. Palette strictly limited to medium cerulean ocean blue #0072a8 and its tints and shades, off-white #fbfcfd, ink grey #13212b and a touch of cobalt blue #3D6FD9 on the pennant only.
